string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of China and one of four direct-administered municipalities in the country. Located in northern China, it has served as a political and cultural centre for centuries and is home to landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and nearby sections of the Great Wall. The city combines historic hutongs and imperial sites with modern business districts and major universities. As the national capital, Beijing hosts central government institutions, museums and international events, including the 2008 and 2022 Olympic Games. Its history, education and cultural life make it a key destination for visitors and researchers.

Shanghai is a direct-administered municipality on the eastern coast of China, located at the mouth of the Yangtze River. It grew from a trading port into one of the largest financial and commercial centres in the world. The city is known for the historic waterfront of the Bund, the modern skyline of Pudong and vibrant districts such as Xintiandi and other central areas. Shanghai also has a strong cultural and educational scene, with museums, theatres and universities. Its economy includes finance, shipping, manufacturing and technology. The mix of colonial-era architecture and contemporary development reflects its role as a global gateway to China.

Chongqing is a direct-administered municipality in southwest China, situated where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet. It is one of the largest municipalities in China by area and population, with a landscape of mountains, rivers and steep urban districts. Chongqing is an important industrial and transportation centre and serves as a gateway to the Three Gorges region. The city is famous for spicy hotpot, night views and historic sites such as Ciqikou. Rapid development, major infrastructure and distinctive geography have made it a significant economic hub in western China.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality in northern China, located near the Bohai Sea and close to Beijing. It is an important port and industrial city with a long history of trade and international contact. Tianjin is known for the Haihe River, historic foreign-style buildings in the Five Great Avenues area and cultural sites such as the Tianjin Museum. The city has developed strength in manufacturing, logistics, finance and education. As part of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, it plays a key role in regional transport and economic development while preserving local traditions and cuisine.
